sdd.audience: the five personas named in [PVD §4](PVD.md): **developer-authors** (the primary audience for the structured editing, AI assistance, and merge surfaces); **tech leads / reviewers** (the audience for the diff- and PR-review-friendly generated documents); **QA / verification engineers** (the audience for the STP and the per-test traceability annotations); **auditors / external stakeholders** (the audience for the self-contained Markdown traceability matrix); and **tooling integrators** (the audience for the JSON-RPC sidecar). This document is also written to be consumable by **AI authoring agents** working through the schema-grounded pipeline described in [PVD §5 #6](PVD.md).

scope.file: the structured source-of-truth that every other component reads or writes.
the XSD schema (and, from Phase 2.5 onwards, the `xs:appinfo` UI-hint vocabulary that drives the schema-driven extension surfaces).
the Jinja2-based renderer that turns `Project.xml` into each spec Markdown document.
the XSD + semantic linter whose findings drive both CI and the in-editor diagnostics.
the per-document Jinja2 templates that own all spec-doc scaffolding (headings, numbering, tables).
the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 sidecar that exposes every parse / render / lint / merge / AI operation to all UI surfaces.
the deterministic three-way structural merger for `Project.xml` (Stage A of the merge pipeline).
the Python AI pipeline: grounding-bundle assembly, intent prompts, response schemas, and the validate-then-retry loop.
the first-class VS Code extension that delivers in-editor authoring, schema-driven views, AI assistance, and AI-mediated merge resolution.
scope.outro: Out of scope for this SDD: the standalone web form (covered by [tools/PLAN_web_form.md](../tools/PLAN_web_form.md)); editor integrations beyond VS Code (PVD §9 roadmap theme); per-test framework annotation conventions, which remain project-specific.

overview.para: `TR` (TraceR) is a repository-native traceability toolkit. A single XML file (`doc/Project.xml`) holds the design, the high-level requirements, the low-level requirements, the test catalogue, and every cross-reference between them. A renderer turns that file into five Markdown documents (SDD, HLRs, LLRs, STP, Traceability Matrix); a linter validates it; a JSON-RPC sidecar exposes the same operations to a VS Code extension and a planned web form; an AI authoring layer drafts and reviews content under a strict validate-then-retry contract; and a structural three-way merger keeps Git merges of `Project.xml` sane.

The unifying design choice (`PVD §5`) is that **the spec documents are an output, not an input**. Every authoring surface edits the structured source and lets the renderer produce the prose. This SDD documents the components that enforce that contract; the SPD ([doc/SDD.md](SPD.md)) documents the *plan* to build them.

The architecture is deliberately **schema-driven from Phase 2.5 onwards** ([PVD §6 Principle 11](PVD.md)). The VS Code extension's tree, code lenses, form panels, document-render commands, and Markdown preview are built at runtime from `tools/project.xsd` UI hints (`xs:appinfo`) and the `<metadata><document>` list, so adding a new generated document or payload section is a schema-and-template change with zero TypeScript involvement. Bespoke widgets and domain-specific lint rules remain the only payload-aware code paths.

Several capabilities are deliberately **deferred to the PVD roadmap themes** ([PVD §9](PVD.md)) and therefore have no module in this SDD: the standalone web form (covered by its own plan); editor breadth beyond VS Code (JetBrains, Neovim, generic LSP); output-format breadth (HTML, PDF, DITA); schema-evolution migration tooling; and the optional `<plan>`-payload phasing overlay. Each is gated on demand and on Phase 1–5.5 having stabilised; when one is adopted, this SDD gains a corresponding module under [SDD §2.1 System Architecture](#21-system-architecture).

definitions.term: The single source of truth. Holds `<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, plus `<metadata>` describing each generated document. Lives at `doc/Project.xml`. Authored through structured surfaces; never edited as raw XML on the critical path.
A top-level child of `<project>` (`<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, or any future schema-declared section like `<plan>`) whose data is rendered into one or more Markdown documents.
A `.md` file under `doc/` produced by the renderer from `Project.xml` plus a Jinja2 template. Listed in `<metadata><document id="…"/>`. Never edited by hand.

`tools/project_io.py` — the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 server that every UI surface calls into. Owns parsing, validation, rendering, AI requests, and the structural merger. Spawned per extension activation; killed on deactivate.

An `xs:appinfo` annotation in `tools/project.xsd` (under the `https://tracer.dev/ui/1` namespace) that tells the extension how to surface a schema element: `ui:treeNode`, `ui:form`, `ui:lens`, `ui:document`. The hint registry is the contract between schema authors and the schema-driven extension surfaces.
The runtime dictionary built by `project_io.parse_to_json` from the XSD's UI hints. Drives the tree view, lens provider, locator, and form-field generator without per-payload TypeScript code.
A `<trace target="…" ref="…"/>` element on an HLR, LLR, or test, naming the upstream item it implements or verifies. The basis for the computed forward and reverse traceability matrix.
An HLR or LLR not referenced by any downstream `<trace>`. Listed explicitly in `Traceability.md`; surfaced as a lint warning and a tree-view badge. Never silently hidden.

The deterministic packed payload (`tools/ai/context.py`) sent to the language model on every AI request: schema subtree, `Schema_Reference.md` excerpt, PVD excerpt, relevant SDD/HLR/LLR context, sibling items, and the lint state of the target. Bounded by `projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens`.

A named AI operation (`draft.hlr`, `expand.hlr_to_llrs`, `review.item`, `merge.body`, …) with its own prompt template (`tools/ai/intents/`) and JSON response schema (`tools/ai/schemas/`). Responses are typed JSON, never raw XML.

The AI pipeline (`tools/ai/pipeline.py`) that parses an AI response against its intent schema, applies it as a JSON Patch on a copy of the tree, runs XSD + lint, and on failure retries with the validator output fed back. After max retries the suggestion is surfaced to the user instead of written.

The deterministic structural three-way merge (`tools/project_merge.py`) over the parsed `Project.xml` tree. Re-keys elements by id, unions non-overlapping additions, unions `<traces>`, recomputes `<counts>`. No AI, no network.

The AI-mediated resolution of residual conflicts left by Stage A: overlapping body edits, divergent trace targets, ID renames, schema-version bumps. Runs through the same validate→retry pipeline as authoring intents.
The `schema_version` attribute on `<project>`. Bumped whenever `Project.xml`'s structure changes in a way existing templates or `render_doc.py` could not consume unchanged.

architecture.intro: The system is a Python core surrounded by editor-native shells. The Python core (`render_doc.py`, `lint_project.py`, `project_merge.py`, `tools/ai/`) is invoked by the long-running JSON-RPC sidecar (`project_io.py`). All UI surfaces — the VS Code extension, the planned web form, AI assistants — speak only to the sidecar; none of them re-implement parsing, rendering, linting, or merging.
architecture.component: the structured source of truth that every other component reads or writes; XSD-validated and lint-validated.
the schema, including (from Phase 2.5) the `xs:appinfo` UI-hint vocabulary that drives the schema-driven extension surfaces. The hint registry is built from this file at sidecar startup.
per-document Jinja2 templates. One per `<metadata><document>` entry. Templates own all spec-doc scaffolding (headings, numbering, tables); payloads carry only content.

the renderer. CLI for batch regeneration plus an importable library API (`render_to_str`, `parse_project_to_dict`) called by the sidecar. Never spawns a sub-process; never writes files outside its `--out` argument.
the linter. CLI plus an importable `lint(tree)` library API. Validates well-formedness, XSD conformance, ID format and uniqueness, broken trace references, and coverage gaps.
the deterministic three-way structural merger (Stage A of the merge pipeline). Operates on the parsed-dict representation from `render_doc.parse_project_to_dict`.
the Python AI pipeline: `context.py` (grounding bundle assembler), `pipeline.py` (validate→retry loop), `intents/` (per-intent prompt templates), `schemas/` (per-intent JSON response schemas).

the JSON-RPC 2.0 sidecar over stdin/stdout. Methods: `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `apply_edit(json_patch)`, `init_project`, `list_documents`, `merge_three_way`, `ai_request(intent, context, target)`. Started lazily on first client call; killed on shutdown.

the VS Code extension. Hosts the tree view, diagnostics, code lenses, form webviews, Markdown preview, walkthrough, `@projectspec` chat participant, and merge editor wiring. Schema-driven from Phase 2.5 onwards.

the standalone web form (planned). Shares the sidecar; outside this SDD's detailed-design scope but listed here so the "one backend, many surfaces" invariant ([PVD §6](PVD.md)) is visible in the architecture.

flow.intro: End-to-end authoring flow (HLR addition shown; LLRs, tests, modules, and merge resolution follow the same shape):
flow.step: The user opens `doc/Project.xml` in VS Code. The extension spawns `tools/project_io.py` and calls `parse_to_json` plus `list_documents` once on activation.
The schema-driven tree provider walks the hint registry returned by `parse_to_json` and contributes one root node per `ui:treeNode`-marked element kind, populated from the parsed payload.
The user clicks "Add HLR" on the HLRs tree node. The extension opens a form webview whose JSON Schema was derived from the relevant XSD subtree plus its `ui:form` hints.

On submit, the webview posts a JSON Patch to the extension, which forwards it to the sidecar's `apply_edit` method. The sidecar applies the patch on a working copy, runs XSD + lint, and (on success) writes the result back to `Project.xml` preserving comments and CDATA via `lxml`.
The extension's file watcher fires on the write; the tree, diagnostics, and code lenses refresh from a fresh `parse_to_json` call.
If `projectXml.previewOnSave` is enabled, the extension calls the sidecar's `render(document_id)` for the affected document and updates the side-by-side Markdown preview pane.

On commit + push + merge, if Git produces a conflict on `doc/Project.xml`, the extension offers `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts`, pulls `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs via `git show`, and calls the sidecar's `merge_three_way` (Stage A). Residual conflicts are routed to the AI pipeline (Stage B) and surfaced in VS Code's three-way merge editor.

design_goals.goal: `Project.xml` is the only authoritative artefact. Generated Markdown documents are an output, never an input. No design element, requirement, or test exists in any other store. From [PVD §6 Principle 1](PVD.md).

Inputs and outputs are text files in the repository. No database, no server, no binary store, no proprietary format. This rules out any feature that would require a runtime service to read the spec. From [PVD §6 Principle 2](PVD.md).

Every payload field is described in `tools/project.xsd` and documented in `Schema_Reference.md` before any template, renderer, or UI consumes it. `schema_version` is bumped on breaking changes. From [PVD §6 Principle 3](PVD.md).

The core renderer and linter use only the Python standard library plus Jinja2; XSD validation falls back gracefully when `lxml` and `xmllint` are absent. No heavy dependencies on the spec-generation hot path. From [PVD §6 Principle 4](PVD.md).

CLI, JSON-RPC sidecar, VS Code extension, web form, and AI assistance all call the same Python functions — directly or via the sidecar. UI layers never re-implement parsing, rendering, linting, or merging. From [PVD §6 Principle 5](PVD.md).

goal.name: No hand-written XML on the critical path

design_goals.goal: Routine authoring is doable end-to-end through the extension's structured surfaces. Any workflow that *requires* the user to edit XML by hand to perform a common task is a bug. From [PVD §6 Principle 6](PVD.md).

goal.name: AI as a co-author, not an oracle

design_goals.goal: AI-generated content is grounded in project data, constrained by typed JSON response schemas, and gated on the same XSD + lint pipeline as manual edits. Every AI write is diff-previewed and logged to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl`. The linter, not the model, is the authority on correctness. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md).

Every broken trace, duplicate ID, or unverified requirement is surfaced by the linter and (in-editor) by a diagnostic. Coverage gaps are explicit rows in the Traceability Matrix. Warnings are never downgraded to keep CI green. From [PVD §6 Principle 8](PVD.md).

`HLR-NNN` and `LLR-XXX-NN` IDs are contracts. They are never renumbered; new IDs take the next free number. Stage A merges honour this when allocating ids to newly-added items on collision. From [PVD §6 Principle 9](PVD.md).
Every behaviour worth describing is captured as an HLR/LLR with at least one bound test. The Traceability Matrix is the contract, not a status report. From [PVD §6 Principle 10](PVD.md).

Adding a new generated document, a new payload section, or a new field is a schema-and-template change — not a TypeScript change. The extension discovers what to render from `tools/project.xsd` UI hints and `<metadata><document>` entries. Bespoke visualisations and domain-specific lint rules are the only payload-aware code paths. From [PVD §6 Principle 11](PVD.md), implemented in SPD Phase 2.5.

Every optional capability fails closed: AI surfaces hide when no language model is available, XSD validation falls back to `xmllint` then to a structural-only pass with a note when `lxml` is absent, and the structured merger refuses rather than guesses when the Git merge base is unavailable. The deterministic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, code lenses, form panels, render, Stage A merge) keep working in every degraded mode. From [PVD §7.1](PVD.md) graceful-degradation contract.

No AI write lands without a diff preview; no merge resolution lands without the user driving the merge editor; every AI-authored edit is logged to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl`; every write goes through the same backup pipeline as a manual edit. "Undo last AI edit" is one click. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md) and the `Trust, transparency, and undo" requirements throughout PVD §5.6 and §5.7.

Grounding bundles never include `.git`, `node_modules`, or any file outside `doc/` and `tools/templates/` by default. AI surfaces are off in untrusted workspaces. The `projectXml.ai.contextAllowList` setting is the only knob that widens the disclosure surface. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md) and the trusted-workspace gating called out in [SPD Phase 5](SPD.md).

module.purpose: is the canonical schema for `doc/Project.xml`: every payload element, attribute, and (from Phase 2.5) the UI-hint vocabulary that drives the schema-driven extension surfaces.
module.responsibility: Constrain the structure of `<project>` and every payload (`<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, plus future schema-declared sections).

Carry UI hints in `xs:appinfo` under the `https://tracer.dev/ui/1` namespace: `ui:treeNode`, `ui:form`, `ui:lens`, `ui:document`. The sidecar distils these into the hint registry consumed by the extension.
Be loadable by `lxml`, `xmllint`, and `xml.etree`. The linter detects and reports hint-vocabulary violations; missing UI hints are warnings, not errors.

interfaces.interface: `tools/render_doc.py` does not consume the XSD directly; it relies on the linter to have validated the document before render. Schema-shape changes that templates depend on require a coordinated template + `render_doc.py` update.

`tools/lint_project.py` validates `Project.xml` against the XSD using `lxml` (preferred) or `xmllint` (fallback), and gracefully degrades to "not validated" with a note when neither is available. UI-hint validation is additional and runs after structural validation succeeds.

`tools/project_io.py` parses the XSD on startup, extracts the UI-hint registry, caches it on the `parse_to_json` response (under `ui_hints_index`), and re-derives a JSON Schema for each form-target subtree on demand.

dependencies.dep: None at runtime; this is a static schema file.
Authoring depends on `xmllint` for local validation; `Schema_Reference.md` is the human-facing reference.

module.purpose: is the document renderer: it turns `doc/Project.xml` plus a Jinja2 template into one Markdown spec document.
module.responsibility: Parse `Project.xml` into a `SimpleNamespace` tree (the `project.*` namespace consumed by every template).

Compute derived projections used by templates: flat lists (`flat_hlrs`, `flat_llrs`, `flat_tests`), id lookups (`hlr_by_id`, `llr_by_id`, `file_of_test`), cross-reference indexes (`hlrs_by_sdd`, `llrs_by_hlr`, `tests_by_hlr`, `tests_by_llr`), coverage-gap lists, and template filters (`gh_slug`).
Render any template against the `<metadata><document>` entry selected by CLI argument; the template owns all document-shape decisions (headings, tables, numbering).

Provide an importable library API (`render_to_str(template, doc_id, project_xml)`, `parse_project_to_dict(project_xml)`) used by the sidecar so the same code path is used by CLI, extension, web form, and AI pipeline.
Provide an `--init` mode that bootstraps a new project's `Project.xml` and `PVD.md` from skeletons.

interfaces.interface: `python3 tools/render_doc.py <template_path> <document_id> [--out <path>]` — render one document. `python3 tools/render_doc.py --init` — bootstrap.

`render_to_str(template_path: Path, document_id: str, project_xml: Path) -> str` — render to a string. `parse_project_to_dict(project_xml: Path) -> dict` — return the raw parsed tree (used by `project_merge.py` and the sidecar's JSON projection). Raises `ProjectXmlError` on any parse / template / metadata error; the CLI converts these to exit codes, library callers catch them directly.

module.purpose: is the structural and semantic linter for `Project.xml`. Its findings drive both CI and the in-editor diagnostics surface.
module.responsibility: Validate well-formedness and XSD conformance against `tools/project.xsd`, using `lxml` (preferred), then `xmllint` (fallback), then a structural-only pass with a "not XSD-validated" note.

Check `<metadata>` shape: every template under `tools/templates/` must have a matching `<document id="…">`; document ids are unique. From Phase 2.5 the required-set is derived from templates, not a hard-coded list.
Check ID format and uniqueness for HLRs (`HLR-NNN`), LLRs (`LLR-XXX-NN`), and test names (free-form but unique within their `<file>`).
Resolve every `<trace>` reference; report broken refs as errors, weak refs (e.g. SDD section numbers that look malformed) as warnings.
Compute coverage gaps: HLRs with no LLR or test linking to them; LLRs with no test linking to them. Report as warnings; the Traceability Matrix template renders them as explicit rows.
Provide an importable `lint(project_xml: Path) -> LintResult` library API; the CLI is a thin wrapper.

interfaces.interface: `python3 tools/lint_project.py [--xml doc/Project.xml]` — prints findings to stdout / stderr; exits non-zero on errors.

`lint(project_xml: Path) -> LintResult` where `LintResult = { errors: list[Finding], warnings: list[Finding], notes: list[Finding], ok: bool }` and each `Finding` carries `message`, `line`, `column`, `xpath`, `code`. The `code` is stable and used by the extension to attach the right Quick Fix.

module.purpose: holds the per-document Jinja2 templates that own all spec-doc scaffolding (titles, headings, numbering, tables, anchors).
module.responsibility: One template per `<metadata><document>` entry. Each consumes the `project.*` namespace exposed by `render_doc.py` and emits Markdown.
Emit anchor `` tags immediately before every `HLR-NNN`, `LLR-XXX-NN`, and `test_…` row so the Traceability template can link to them.
Never invent payload fields. Adding a new field requires the schema, the renderer, and the template to be updated together.

interfaces.interface: `SDD.md.j2`, `HLRs.md.j2`, `LLRs.md.j2`, `STP.md.j2`, `Traceability.md.j2`. New documents add a sibling template plus a `<metadata><document id="…">` entry; from Phase 2.5 the extension picks them up automatically.
`PVD.md.template` is consumed by `render_doc.py --init` to seed `doc/PVD.md` for new projects.

dependencies.dep: The data surface exposed by `tools/render_doc.py` (see its module above).

module.purpose: is the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 sidecar that exposes every parse / render / lint / merge / AI operation to all UI surfaces. The "one backend, many surfaces" guarantee ([PVD §6 Principle 5](../doc/PVD.md)) is enforced here.
module.responsibility: Speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout. Methods: `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `apply_edit`, `init_project`, `list_documents`, `merge_three_way`, `ai_request`, `subscribe_changes`, `shutdown`.

Be the only writer to `Project.xml` (via `apply_edit`); UI surfaces send JSON Patch ops, the sidecar applies them on the parsed tree, runs XSD + lint, and serializes back via `lxml` so that comments, CDATA, attribute order, and whitespace are preserved.
Be process-safe: started lazily on first client call, killed on `shutdown` or extension deactivate; survives a single failed request without crashing the session.

interfaces.interface: `render(document_id: str) -> { markdown, source_template }` — renders one document. The Markdown preview surface calls this; it never writes a file.

`parse_to_json() -> { project: ParsedNode, ui_hints_index, metadata, counts }` — generic projection of the whole tree plus the hint registry. The schema-driven tree, lens, and locator providers consume this exclusively.

`apply_edit(patch: JsonPatch, expect_clean: bool = true) -> { ok, lint, residual_diff }` — atomically apply, validate, write. Refuses if `expect_clean` is true and the in-editor text buffer is dirty (the extension prompts the user to save or discard).
`init_project(name, short_name, author) -> { paths_written }` — wraps `render_doc.py --init`.
`list_documents() -> [{ id, title, source, template, ui_document }]` — enumerates `<metadata><document>` entries; the extension's "Render <Doc>" command palette contributions are derived from this.

`ai_request(intent: str, context: dict, target: dict) -> { patch?, suggestion?, validations: [Finding], retries }` — delegates to `tools/ai/pipeline.py`. Used by the chat participant, the right-click "with AI" actions, and the merge resolver's Stage B.
`subscribe_changes() -> stream` — pushes notifications when the file watcher detects an out-of-band change to `Project.xml`. The extension uses this to refresh the tree.

error_handling.case: Returns a JSON-RPC error with `code = -32001` and the line/column of the failure; the extension surfaces it as a top-level diagnostic on the file.

`apply_edit` is serialised per session. A concurrent edit landing during validation causes the patch to be rebased on the new tree and re-validated; if rebase fails, the call returns `code = -32010` ("conflicting concurrent edit") and the caller retries.
`ai_request` returns `code = -32020` ("no language model available"); the extension hides the AI surfaces gracefully per [PVD §7.1](../doc/PVD.md) graceful-degradation contract.

module.purpose: is the deterministic three-way structural merger over `Project.xml` (Stage A of the merge pipeline described in SPD Phase 5.5).
module.responsibility: Re-key elements by their stable ids (`HLR-NNN`, `LLR-XXX-NN`, test names, module paths) so a merge is position-independent.
Union additions when ids do not collide; on collision where both sides are new, allocate the next free id to one side (existing ids never move, per [PVD §6 Principle 9](../doc/PVD.md)).
Union `<traces>` entries by `(target, ref)` tuple, deduping.
Recompute `<metadata>/<counts>` from the merged tree.
Take the structurally-equivalent side when whitespace, comment, or attribute-order differences are the only divergence.

Emit residual conflicts (genuinely overlapping body edits, divergent trace targets, ID renames, schema-version bumps) as a structured list rather than fixing them; the AI pipeline (Stage B) consumes the list.
Refuse and report rather than guess when the merge base is unavailable (rebase-in-progress, octopus merges, cherry-picks without a base).

interfaces.interface: `merge(base: dict, ours: dict, theirs: dict) -> { merged: dict, residual_conflicts: [Conflict] }` where each input is the parsed-dict representation from `render_doc.parse_project_to_dict`. The merged tree is serialised through the same `lxml`-based write-back path as `apply_edit` so comments and CDATA are preserved.

dependencies.dep: `tools/lint_project.py` for the post-merge lint pass that gates acceptance.

module.purpose: is the AI pipeline. It assembles a grounding bundle from project data, calls the language model with a typed JSON response schema, and validates the response through the same XSD + lint pipeline as manual edits.
module.responsibility: `context.py` — `build_ai_context(target) -> bundle` packs the schema subtree, `Schema_Reference.md` excerpt, PVD excerpt, SDD/HLR/LLR context appropriate to the intent, sibling items as style anchors, and the lint state of the target. A deterministic packer enforces `projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens`; the schema and the user intent are never dropped.

`pipeline.py` — implements the validate→retry loop: parse JSON against the intent's response schema, translate to a JSON Patch, apply on a copy of the tree, run XSD + `lint_project.lint`, and on failure retry with the findings as feedback. After max retries surface the suggestion + the failures to the user.

`intents/` — one Markdown file per intent, holding the system prompt and few-shot examples grounded in the schema. Authoring intents: `draft.hlr`, `draft.llr`, `draft.test`, `draft.module`, `expand.hlr_to_llrs`, `review.item`, `suggest.traces`, `gap.fix`. Merge intents: `merge.body`, `merge.trace`, `merge.rename`, `merge.schema_bump`.
`schemas/` — one JSON Schema per intent describing the shape of a valid response (Pydantic-validated). The deterministic translator that maps the JSON to a JSON Patch lives next to each schema.
Append a provenance entry to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` per accepted/rejected suggestion (timestamp, intent, model, prompt hash, accept/reject, validator state).

interfaces.interface: `build_ai_context(target: TargetSpec) -> Bundle` (in `context.py`). `run(intent: str, context: Bundle, target: TargetSpec) -> AiResult` (in `pipeline.py`) — returns either an applied JSON Patch + lint result, or a rejected suggestion + the validator findings that blocked it.
The sidecar exposes `ai_request` (see project_io module above), which is the only entry point UI surfaces use; the TS side never imports `tools/ai/` directly.

dependencies.dep: `tools/project.xsd` and `Schema_Reference.md` for the grounding bundle's schema and authoring-guidance sections.
The host's language model (via the VS Code Language Model API on the TS side, never called directly from Python).

error_handling.case: Auto-retry with the parser error fed back as a correction prompt; counts against the configured retry budget.

Auto-retry with the new findings fed back. If the candidate introduces no *new* errors compared to the pre-edit state, it is accepted (an unrelated pre-existing warning does not block the suggestion).
Surface the original suggestion + the validator failures to the user instead of writing it; never silently apply.
Return an `AiResult` with `kind = "no-model"`. UI surfaces hide themselves; the linter, renderer, and Stage A merge keep working unchanged.

module.purpose: is the first-class VS Code extension that turns `Project.xml` into a structured editing surface and is the primary delivery vehicle for the in-editor authoring, schema-driven views, AI assistance, and AI-mediated merge resolution called out in [PVD §5 / §7.1](../doc/PVD.md).
module.responsibility: Activate on workspaces containing `doc/Project.xml`. Spawn `tools/project_io.py` once per session and route every operation through it; never parse, render, lint, or merge `Project.xml` itself.

Contribute the "Project Spec" Activity Bar view, the Markdown preview pane, the form webviews, the Walkthrough, the `@projectspec` chat participant, the merge editor integration, and the status bar item.
From Phase 2.5 onwards, build all generic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, lenses, locator, render commands) at runtime from the `ui_hints_index` and `<metadata><document>` list returned by the sidecar.
Declare `extensionDependencies` on `redhat.vscode-xml` so the user gets XSD-backed XML editing (syntax, outline, completion) for free.
Contribute every `projectXml.*` setting through `contributes.configuration` (see Data Dictionary §Settings for the authoritative list and defaults).

Be `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"`: AI surfaces are off until the workspace is trusted; the deterministic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, lenses, forms, render, Stage A merge) keep working in untrusted mode.

interfaces.interface: `workspaceContains:doc/Project.xml`, `onLanguage:xml` (filtered to `Project.xml`), and the `onCommand:projectXml.*` family.

TypeScript, `@vscode/extension` API, esbuild for bundling, mocha + `@vscode/test-electron` for tests. Webviews use React + react-jsonschema-form for form panels; the bundle is shared with the planned web form to avoid duplication.

dependencies.dep: The host's Python interpreter, located via `projectXml.pythonPath`, then the Microsoft Python extension's interpreter API, then `python3`/`python` on PATH.
The host's Language Model API (`vscode.lm.selectChatModels`) for AI surfaces; absent implies graceful degradation.

module.title: Project Spec tree view
module.purpose: contributes the "Project Spec" Activity Bar view that gives every payload a structured outline with inline status badges. From Phase 2.5 it is built entirely from the schema's UI hints, with no per-payload TypeScript.
module.responsibility: Walk `ui_hints_index.treeNodes` and emit one root node per `ui:treeNode`-marked element kind, populated from the parsed payload returned by `parse_to_json`.
Annotate each node with a count badge and surface lint- derived status badges (`⚠`, `❌`) on items with coverage gaps or broken refs.

Provide context-menu commands: `Edit`, `Reveal in XML`, `Add child …`, `Delete`, `Render this section`, `Draft / Expand / Review with AI`. The set of available commands per node is derived from the hint registry, not hard-coded per element kind.
Locate elements in the underlying XML for `Reveal in XML` via the generic locator (`util/locator.ts`), which takes `(elementName, idAttr, idValue)` from the hint registry.

interfaces.interface: `projectXml.tree` registered against the `projectXml-explorer` view container in `contributes.viewsContainers`.
Subscribes to `projectXml.fileChanged` (workspace file watcher on `doc/Project.xml`) and to the sidecar's `subscribe_changes` stream; debounced refresh.

module.title: Diagnostics and Quick Fixes
module.purpose: mirrors lint findings into the Problems panel as VS Code `Diagnostic` objects, with payload-agnostic Quick Fixes for the most common findings.
module.responsibility: Translate each lint `Finding` to a `Diagnostic` using the xpath/line/column carried by the finding; preserve the finding's stable `code` so Quick Fixes can target it.

Provide a `CodeActionProvider` whose Quick Fixes are table-driven from the finding's `code`: "Replace ref with…" picker for broken-trace findings, "Renumber as …" for ID-format errors, "Insert standard `<document>` row" for missing-document warnings, "Create stub test entry" for missing-test warnings, plus an "AI: suggest correct ref" fix on broken-trace findings when AI is enabled.

interfaces.interface: `projectXml-lint` collection; cleared and rebuilt on each lint pass.
Registered for `language: xml` filtered to `Project.xml`. Returns the union of generic + AI fixes that apply to the findings on the requested range.

dependencies.dep: Sidecar `apply_edit` (Quick Fixes apply through the same write path as form edits).
The AI participant module (for the AI-suggest variant of each fix).

module.title: Code lenses
module.purpose: decorates schema-marked elements in `Project.xml` with inline status and click-through actions.
module.responsibility: Walk `ui_hints_index.lenses` and attach the named lens kind (`coverage`, `tracesCount`, custom) to every matching element. From Phase 2.5 the lens provider has zero hard-coded element selectors.
Render compact summaries (e.g. "3 LLRs · 5 tests" on an HLR) plus action lenses (`Edit`, `Preview section`, `🪄 AI`).
Resolve click targets through the generic locator so "jump to LLR-PCL-04" works for any schema-declared id attribute.

interfaces.interface: Registered for `language: xml` filtered to `Project.xml`. Lazily computes lens text from the cached `ui_hints_index` and the latest `parse_to_json` payload.

module.title: Form panels and Markdown preview
module.purpose: hosts the single-item form webviews used to edit one payload element at a time, plus the side-by-side Markdown preview pane.
module.responsibility: Open one form panel per `Edit`/`Add` action. The form's JSON Schema comes from the sidecar's `parse_to_json` response, which derives it from the relevant XSD subtree plus per-field `ui:form` hints.
On submit, post a JSON Patch to the extension which forwards it to `apply_edit`. On `apply_edit` returning a clean lint, the extension closes the panel and refreshes the tree.
Handle dirty-buffer collisions: if `Project.xml` is open in a text editor with unsaved changes, prompt the user to save or discard before applying the patch.
Render the Markdown preview by calling sidecar `render` for the affected document and writing the result to a virtual document; honour `projectXml.previewOnSave`.
Expose a "Draft this field with AI" button next to long Markdown fields; the AI insertion goes into the field, not straight to disk.

interfaces.interface: `form.ready`, `form.submit`, `form.cancel`, `form.aiDraftField`. Bundle is React + RJSF; built once and shared with the planned web form (PLAN_web_form.md).
Uses VS Code's built-in Markdown preview command (`markdown.showPreviewToSide`) against a virtual `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` URI served by an in-memory content provider.

dependencies.dep: Shared RJSF bundle (built by the same Vite step as the web form).

module.title: Guided authoring (Walkthrough)
module.purpose: contributes the VS Code Walkthrough that steps a new user through bootstrapping a project and filling each payload in order. The IDE-native equivalent of the web form's wizard.
module.responsibility: Provide seven steps: bootstrap, PVD, SDD, HLRs, LLRs, tests, render & commit. Each step has Markdown content, a "Run command" link, and an automatic completion check (usually file-state or count-based).
Each step's "Run command" link can optionally be "Run command with AI", which pre-drafts the section through the authoring intents (Phase 5) rather than opening an empty form.

interfaces.interface: Registered under `contributes.walkthroughs` in the extension's `package.json`. Step IDs are stable so VS Code can persist completion state across sessions.

dependencies.dep: All command modules under `commands/` (each step ends in a command invocation).
The AI participant module (for the "with AI" variants).

module.title: AI participant and merge surface
module.purpose: hosts the `@projectspec` chat participant, the right-click "with AI" actions, and the merge editor integration. The TypeScript side of the AI pipeline; the heavy lifting lives in `tools/ai/`.
module.responsibility: Register the chat participant via `vscode.chat.createChatParticipant` with the `/draft-hlr`, `/expand`, `/review`, `/gap-fill`, and `/resolve-conflicts` slash commands.
Translate every chat / right-click / Quick Fix invocation into an `ai_request` call on the sidecar; surface the result through a diff preview before any write.

Detect a conflicted `doc/Project.xml` via the `git` extension API; expose `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts`; pull `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs via `git show`; call the sidecar's `merge_three_way`; open the result in VS Code's three-way merge editor with each AI-resolved region badged "✨ AI suggestion".

Honour `projectXml.ai.enabled`, `projectXml.merge.enabled`, and `projectXml.merge.aiResidualResolution`; the last must be forced off when `ai.enabled` is false. Hide every AI surface cleanly when `vscode.lm.selectChatModels` returns no models.
Never auto-apply: the diff preview (for authoring) and the merge editor (for merge resolution) are the only commit surfaces.

interfaces.interface: Pre-populates VS Code's three-way merge editor with the Stage A merged candidate; each Stage B suggestion is a distinct region the user accepts or rejects.
Appends one entry per AI-resolved region or per authoring suggestion to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` (timestamp, intent, model, prompt hash, accept/reject, validator state).

dependencies.dep: `vscode.chat.*`, `vscode.lm.*`, the `git` extension API, the merge editor API.

error_handling.case: All AI surfaces become invisible (commands hidden, chat participant unregistered, Quick Fix variants suppressed). Stage A merge keeps working without modification.
`untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` blocks AI activation; a warning notification explains the gating once per session.
The merge resolver refuses with a notification ("Stage A requires the Git merge base; falling back to manual resolution") rather than silently picking one side.

type.name: ParsedNode
type.summary: Generic JSON projection of a single XML element returned by parse_to_json. The TypeScript side never re-parses the schema.

field.name: tag
field.desc: The element's local name (e.g. 'hlr', 'llr', 'module').

field.name: attrs
field.desc: The element's attributes verbatim.

field.name: text
field.desc: The element's text content (CDATA-decoded), if any.

field.name: children
field.desc: Direct children grouped by tag name; preserves order within each group.

field.name: xpath
field.desc: XPath into the source `Project.xml`, used by the locator and diagnostics.

type.name: LintResult
type.summary: Aggregate result of a single lint pass.

field.name: errors
field.desc: Hard failures; CI exits non-zero on any error.

field.name: warnings
field.desc: Coverage gaps, weak refs, missing optional metadata.

field.name: notes
field.desc: Informational (e.g. 'lxml not available; structural-only validation').

field.name: ok
field.desc: True iff `errors` is empty.

type.name: Finding
type.summary: One lint finding; the unit the extension turns into a Diagnostic.

field.name: code
field.desc: Stable identifier (e.g. 'broken-trace', 'id-format', 'no-test'); the Quick Fix table is keyed on this.

field.name: message
field.desc: Human-readable message.

field.name: line
field.desc: 1-based line number in `Project.xml`.

field.name: column
field.desc: 1-based column.

field.name: xpath
field.desc: XPath of the offending element/attribute.

type.name: UiHintsIndex
type.summary: Distilled UI-hint registry derived from `tools/project.xsd`'s `xs:appinfo` annotations. Drives every schema-driven extension surface.

field.name: treeNodes
field.desc: One per `ui:treeNode`-marked element kind; carries label expression, idAttr, group.

field.name: forms
field.desc: Per element kind, the field hints (text, textarea, enum, ref:HLR, ref:LLR, cdata) used to generate the JSON Schema for the form webview.

field.name: lenses
field.desc: One per `ui:lens`-marked element kind; identifies which named lens kind to attach (coverage, tracesCount, custom:<name>).

field.name: documents
field.desc: One per `ui:document`-marked `metadata/document`; marks renderable targets and supplies preview metadata.

type.name: JsonPatch
type.summary: RFC 6902 JSON Patch op exchanged between the extension and the sidecar's apply_edit.

field.name: path
field.desc: JSON pointer into the parsed-tree representation; the sidecar resolves to an XML location for write-back.

field.name: value
field.desc: Op-dependent payload.

type.name: Bundle
type.summary: Grounding bundle assembled per AI request. The deterministic packer enforces projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens; schema and user intent are never dropped.

field.name: schema_excerpt
field.desc: Relevant XSD subtree for the intent's target.

field.name: authoring_guide
field.desc: Relevant subtree of `Schema_Reference.md`.

field.name: pvd_excerpt
field.desc: First N kb of `doc/PVD.md`.

field.name: sdd_context
field.desc: Slim list or full module/component depending on intent.

field.name: hlr_context
field.desc: Slim id+name list or full HLR depending on intent.

field.name: llr_context
field.desc: Slim id+text list or full LLR depending on intent.

field.name: siblings
field.desc: Sibling items in the same scope (style anchors).

field.name: lint_state
field.desc: Current findings on the target.

field.name: user_intent
field.desc: The user's chat message or command argument; never dropped by the packer.

type.name: Conflict
type.summary: A residual conflict left by Stage A for the AI pipeline (Stage B) to resolve.

field.name: xpath
field.desc: Where in the merged tree the conflict lives.

field.name: base
field.desc: Snapshot from the merge base.

field.name: ours
field.desc: Snapshot from our side.

field.name: theirs
field.desc: Snapshot from their side.

constant.name: projectXml.xmlPath
constant.purpose: Workspace-relative path to the source-of-truth XML.

constant.name: projectXml.toolsDir
constant.purpose: Directory containing the Python sidecar and helpers.

constant.name: projectXml.pythonPath
constant.purpose: Override interpreter; empty defers to the Microsoft Python extension, then `python3`/`python` on PATH.

constant.name: projectXml.previewOnSave
constant.purpose: Re-render the affected document into the side preview on save.

constant.name: projectXml.warningsAsErrors
constant.purpose: Treat lint warnings as errors in the Problems panel.

constant.name: projectXml.showCoverageBadges
constant.purpose: Render coverage status badges in the tree view.

constant.name: projectXml.autoLintOnChange
constant.purpose: Re-run lint automatically on file change.

constant.name: projectXml.ai.enabled
constant.purpose: Master switch for the AI authoring layer (PVD §5.6).

constant.name: projectXml.ai.preferredModel
constant.purpose: Empty defers to the user's default Copilot Chat model.

constant.name: projectXml.ai.maxRetries
constant.purpose: Validator-feedback retry budget per AI request.

constant.name: projectXml.ai.autoApplyValidated
constant.purpose: Skip the diff preview for fully-validated suggestions; off by default.

constant.name: projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens
constant.purpose: Hard cap on the grounding bundle; the deterministic packer drops largest optional sections first.

constant.name: projectXml.ai.contextAllowList
constant.purpose: File-glob whitelist for the grounding bundle's context sources.

constant.name: projectXml.merge.enabled
constant.purpose: Master switch for the structured-merge feature; off hides the merge surface entirely.

constant.name: projectXml.merge.aiResidualResolution
constant.purpose: Enable Stage B (AI-mediated residual resolution); forced off when `ai.enabled` is false.

data_dictionary.other: The repository layout for the extension itself (TypeScript source tree, test fixtures, build assets) is project-conventional and described in [SPD §7](SPD.md). It is not reproduced here because its precise shape is delivery-phase scaffolding rather than a design contract — the design contract is the responsibilities and interfaces declared per module above.
